label: rem:substrate-gm-torsion
title: The substrate parameter as a $\mathbb{G}_m$-section: torsion, specialisation, and the $q = 1$ boundary
html:
The substrate parameter operates as an element of \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1}) \cong k^\times, establishing the fibre coordinate on a \mathbb{G}_m-family. This parameter must strictly avoid the torsion subgroup of \mathbb{G}_m.

The multiplicative group scheme. The substrate parameter evaluates as a section q \colon M \to \mathbb{G}_m(k) where \mathbb{G}_m(k) = k^\times. The \mathbb{G}_m-family of operators

  d_q = q^{-1}d + (1 - q^{-1})\pi_V \circ d

defines a universal deformation scaling under the tautological coordinate on \mathbb{G}_m = \mathrm{Spec}\mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]. A base change along a ring homomorphism \iota \colon \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}] \to k specialises this family rigidly to the quantum group stationed at q_0 = \iota(q).

Torsion points of the multiplicative group. Roots of unity form the torsion subgroup:

  \mathbb{G}_m[n] = \mu_n = \{\zeta \in k^\times : \zeta^n = 1\},
  \qquad
  \mathbb{G}_m[\mathrm{tors}] = \mu_\infty = \bigcup_{n \geq 1} \mu_n.

The rigid axiom controlling the substrate parameter dictates:

  q(p) \notin \mu_\infty(k)
  \qquad\text{for all } p \in M.

The section q must remain anchored entirely within the non-torsion locus \mathbb{G}_m \setminus \mu_\infty.

Necessity of torsion avoidance. At a strict torsion point q_0 = e^{2\pi i m/n}:

  1. The quantum dimension [n]_{q_0} = 0 zeroes out.
  2. The Frobenius pairing degenerates entirely on V_{(n-1)/2}.
  3. The fundamental QOU non-degeneracy axiom collapses.
  4. The representation category abruptly truncates into a modular tensor category (matching a Chern--Simons TQFT).

The anchor q_0 = 1 constitutes the universal torsion point. While quantum integers [k]_1 = k avoid vanishing, the comultiplication turns cocommutative and the braiding degrades into symmetric swapping.

The projective compactification. Embedding \mathbb{G}_m \hookrightarrow \mathbb{P}^1 defines two absolute boundaries. At q = 0, the operator d_q hits an undefined q^{-1} pole; the spatial differential diverges. At q = \infty, d_q \to \pi_V \circ d; spatial mechanics vanish entirely, isolating purely the vertical Reeb dynamic. Under \mathbb{C}, torsion points blanket \mathbb{G}_m densely. Under \mathbb{R}, torsion points limit to \{1, -1\}; the physical substrate q > 1 cleanly occupies the torsion-free ray (1, \infty).

The q = 1 limit as torsion specialisation. The NS regularity problem effectively tests the extension of a valid non-torsion section q \colon M \to \mathbb{G}_m^{\mathrm{nt}} directly into the universal torsion point q = 1. The Neron model of the abelian scheme controls this exact extension. Because the Frobenius--Hopf architecture operates as a parameterised family of Hopf algebras, not a simple \mathbb{G}_m-torsor, the obstruction directly populates the special fibre:

  \mathrm{obs}(q \to 1)
   \in 
  \Phi_{q=1}(\mathbb{G}_m).

Connection to the NS obstruction. The NS obstruction class \kappa_n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B}) is bound to the banding sheaf \mathcal{B} = \mathcal{O}_M^\times. Consequently,

  \kappa_n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m).

The specialisation q \to 1 applies exactly as a pullback:

  \kappa_n\big|_{q=1}
   \in 
  H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m)
  \xrightarrow{ \mathrm{sp}_{q=1}}
  H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mu_\infty).

The specialisation map factors precisely through the Kummer sequence. The obstruction definitively persists if and only if \kappa_n remains not divisible by n in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) for any finite n.

On the Descartes universe (\chi(A) = -6), the motivic perpetual obstruction theorem commands that the specialisation \kappa_0|_{q = \zeta_n} registers as non-zero at every primitive root avoiding \gcd(n, 6) = 1. The NS obstruction categorically cannot collapse.
